name: 2035 S. Prairie Avenue — the brick-and-frame rear building behind 2035 (district draft; refined by T-1938)

grade.why: Known from maps or written records; no picture of it has been found.

documented_range.note: The draft claims the 1904 target and no more: the 1911 sheet draws the building and the T-1842 census rules it present in 1904 (present_as_mapped). Its building and loss dates are the per-building ticket's to read.

placement.position_note: The rear corner of the main body's rectangle (lot frame u 0.750, v -3.250 m from the middle of the rear lot line), through the T-1250 fit of the sheet: the sheet's georeference carries no independent check: its own fit residual is 0.05 m RMS on its control crossings, a similarity on two degrees of freedom that says little away from them, plus about a pixel (0.19 m) of trace on this coarser copy. Rotation 179.364 degrees turns the plan's u axis onto the lot's own rear-to-street line.
placement.symbolic_location: 2035 S. Prairie Avenue, parcel prairie_2035 (data/street_grid/1904.json), east side of Prairie Avenue, Prairie Avenue, 20th to 22nd Street (Sanborn 1911 vol. 3 sheet 35).

footprint.note: The main body: the largest rectangle that fits inside the traced main part (u toward the street, v along the front). The building's other rectangles are in draft_plan.

stories.note: The census reading 'A rear building of brick first storey and frame above (lettered BRICK 1ST), two and three storeys, joined to a 2-storey brick building on the alley at the corner': 2 storeys.

construction.note: The trace's fabric colour on the main part: brick.

parts.from: s35fp-2035-b2 outline (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 81% of its fill

draft_plan.note: Rectangles fitted inside the traced parts by the rules' fit (cell 0.25 m, at most 3 a part, to 90% cover): s35fp-2035-b2 outline (main, brick), rectangle 1 of that part; the part's rectangles cover 81% of its fill. Roles: the main part's largest rectangle is the main body; a shallow rectangle at the front is a bay; the sheet's ranges, porches and stone fronts keep their roles. Storeys per piece and roof per piece are the draft rules' (reconstructed).

draft_elevation.note: RECONSTRUCTED by the draft rules, family row 'service' overlaid with the frontage row: 2035, the 21st Street corner of the 1869 limestone row, Mrs. H. O. Stone's in February 1904: the register's family ('corner of limestone row') matches no draft family, so the row's bracketed flat cornice is set here to keep the shared line; its door toward the corner. Its mixed brick-and-frame rear building stands as the sheet traces it. The census does not read that building's use, so it stands as an outbuilding, not a stable. Heights are the rules' starting values inside RECONSTRUCTION-RULES.md's ranges; bays, entrance side, chimneys and dormers are counts the family rules choose, and the seed 1723291861 only tints the fabric inside +-6 %. Liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-east-2352.

draft.note: The draft's own provenance: the pass that wrote it, the rows it read and the tickets that replace it attribute by attribute under this id.

function.note: The 1911 sheet reads 'A rear building of brick first storey and frame above (lettered BRICK 1ST), two and three storeys, joined to a 2-storey brick building on the alley at the corner'. Mixed fabric drawn in 1911, backcast to 1904; its use is not read. Carried to 1904 on the T-1842 census ruling (present_as_mapped).

citations.citation: Sanborn Map Company. Insurance Maps of Chicago, Illinois, Volume 3. New York: Sanborn Map Company, 1911. Sheet 35.
what_it_supplies: Footprints, lots and street widths from 20th to 22nd Street between Indiana and Calumet, as of 1911, at the copy's coarser resolution
The position of Twentieth Street, which is vacated between Indiana and Calumet today
what_it_does_not_supply: Anything as of 1904 on its own authority. It is a 1911 survey; Glessner House's reading that everything on sheets 20, 28 and 35 but 1609-1611 and 1620 Prairie stood in 1904 is attributed guidance, recorded in that README, and not checked by this record
A construction date for any building it draws
Elevations, grades, curb heights or fill depths -- no Sanborn sheet carries a level
Architecture above the footprint beyond its story count, material colour and roof symbol
Any lake edge: the sheet ends at Calumet Avenue

research_note: A DISTRICT DRAFT (T-2352, the owner's district pass of 2026-10-08): a serviceable first model, complete from the street, the walks, the alley and the air, that T-1938 refines in place under this same id. Written by tools/draft_prairie_1904.py from the sheet 35 trace (s35fp-2035-b2), the T-1842 census (s35-2035-rear) and the T-1837 register row frontage-35-083; every height, roof, opening and feature is the draft rules' reconstruction (data/components/prairie_1904/draft_prairie_1904.json; liberty L-draft-prairie-20-22-east-2352).
